# Joy v0.17.0 — first release you can actually install

Earlier tags (v0.5.0, v0.8.0, v0.16.0) never produced a Release: the macOS Intel
build used the `macos-13` runner image, which GitHub retired on 2025-12-04, so
that job sat in the queue until the run was cancelled and the dependent `release`
job was skipped. The build now runs on `macos-15-intel`. **This is the first
version with downloadable binaries.**

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, extract, run:

```bash
tar -xzf joy-v0.17.0-<your-target>.tar.gz && chmod +x joy
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=… ./joy dashboard        # -> http://localhost:7777
```

Four targets: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`,
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
No API key? Ollama runs fully offline (`JOY_PROVIDER=ollama`).
Docker: `docker build -t joy .` then
`docker run --rm -p 7777:7777 -v joy-state:/home/joy/.joy joy`.

## Highlights

**Inspectable memory.** Every turn writes one append-only ledger row. Open a row
in the dashboard's memory drawer to see that turn's full entry stream — the
retrieval gate's decision, tool calls and timings, which model answered, token
usage. The `<home>/memory` OKF bundle carries a rebuildable FTS5 index; a
background worker consolidates and mirrors it. The memory center adds a library
with `ledger:…` chips back to source turns, a six-section context meter, and
on-demand `/compact [focus]`.

**The dashboard speaks English and Chinese.** 266 strings go through `t()`, with
`data-i18n*` attributes for static markup; a sidebar button switches language
and remembers it, and a fresh browser follows `navigator.language`.
`just check-i18n` fails on missing, unused or placeholder-mismatched
translations. The dashboard also remembers which conversation you were reading
across reloads, and returns to your previous scroll position when you switch back.

**Turns finish their own work.** When the step cap cuts a turn off, a built-in
gate checks the todo list and continues (up to `JOY_AUTO_CONTINUE_MAX`),
carrying working memory and a fresh step slice instead of restarting from
`chat_log`. When the budget is genuinely gone, the reply says what is left and
`traces/*.jsonl` records `steps` / `continues` / `unfinished`.

**Deterministic replay evals.** `joy eval --replay` pins event ordering for
compaction, approval timeouts, streamed output and MCP reconnects. Events match
as an ordered subsequence; a case that asserts nothing is refused on load.
`just check` now includes `eval-replay`.

**Cheaper turns.** Split system prompt with an Anthropic cache breakpoint and
cached-token accounting, thin/full souls, skill catalog with on-demand bodies
(`read_skill`), deferred tool loading (`find_tools`), oldest-first result
trimming. 29 built-in tools (21 always on, 8 behind switches) plus MCP servers.

**Recovery and safety.** Recovered tasks recheck acceptance and record spend;
tool batches persist intent before execution, and recovery suspends batches with
unknown results for reconciliation rather than replaying them; background jobs
use restart-safe IDs. Batched subagents are read-only and carry distinct session
names. Configuration now has one source of truth — `just check-config-docs`
fails unless every `JOY_*` the code reads appears in `.env.example` and both
configuration docs.

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) / [CHANGELOG.zh.md](CHANGELOG.zh.md).

## Known limitations

- Discord / WeChat / Lark gateways are implemented but have never been connected
  to those platforms. Only Telegram has.
- File writes and shell execution are off by default (`JOY_WRITE=1` /
  `JOY_EXEC=1`); the writable boundary is Unix-only for now.
- The Homebrew formula now carries the real v0.17.0 sha256, but the tap itself
  (and the PyPI / npm channels) is not published yet.
- Full list: [docs/limitations.md](docs/limitations.md).

If anything above does not match what you see, please open an issue — a failed
install is more useful to this project than a star. Releases are planned every
1–2 weeks; **Watch → Custom → Releases** if you only want those.
